title: Healer: Original Research-Informed Assessment Question Bank
intendedUse: English-language educational app prototype and voluntary self-reflection for adults aged 18 or older. Not for diagnosis, clinical screening decisions, treatment selection, emergency triage, hiring, grading, or eligibility decisions.
importantSafetyAndMethodology: All 170 core questions and four additional support questions are newly written. They are research-informed content, not validated instruments, translations, or authorized adaptations of the cited measures.
The source review was a targeted review of public health guidance, owner-hosted documentation, and research abstracts on 2026-10-16; it was not a systematic review or a clinical validation study.
The screenshots establish the 17 module names only. They do not reveal the original Healer questions, algorithms, scoring rules, or psychometric properties.

The supplied abc.json is a structural template, not an executable JSON Schema. A trailing question mark in its field names is treated as an optional-field marker; production keys do not include that question mark.

Source references support the choice of topics, not the validity of the new wording, recall periods, response options, score weights, or sums. These design decisions are author-created and require testing.
For every assessment, validForClinicalDecisions is false and officialReferenceBands.enabled is false. Do not import published cutoffs into these original questions.

Assessment names match the screenshot catalog for integration. User-facing pages must identify them as unvalidated self-reflection activities; the IQ Test must display Reasoning practice, not IQ measurement.
Show the full timeframe and instructions before each module and keep them accessible with each question. Question stems must not be displayed without their recall context.
Each question is single-choice. Self-report modules have no right or wrong answers. Only the ten reasoning puzzles have correct answers, represented by option score 1.

Allow users to skip a question, choose an external Not applicable / Cannot judge action, or stop without penalty. Store such responses as missing, never as the lowest scored option. Do not preselect answers.

Self-report numerical sums are optional descriptive response summaries only, not measures of clinical severity, probability, functioning, intelligence, or treatment response. Item-level answers should remain visible.
Do not combine scores across modules. The personality module reports five separate two-item means. The autism module reports individual answers only and has no total score.
All reverse coding is already applied in options[].score. Never reverse a response again. The min and max for profile-only modules refer to each displayed component, not an overall sum.

Depression has ten core items plus dep_11 and dep_12; Sleep has ten core items plus slp_11; Relationships has ten core items plus rel_11. These four extra support questions are unscored; all their numeric option scores are deliberately zero.
Support triggers use selected option IDs, not numeric scores. Evaluate them immediately when an answer is selected, even when the questionnaire is incomplete. Never wait for a total score.
No, a skipped answer, Prefer not to answer, and a low total cannot establish safety. General crisis and support access must remain available in every module, not only Depression.
A true human_review_required flag describes a need for qualified review, not an existing service. This file does not monitor users, summon help, or create a staffed clinical response pathway.

Before real use, a qualified mental health professional must review content and support workflows. Configure and verify support contacts for each deployment country; do not present U.S. numbers as global resources.

Protect sensitive answers: explain collection and sharing, collect only necessary information, provide deletion controls, and do not automatically notify partners, employers, teachers, or family members.
Do not force disclosure of trauma or self-harm details. Offer a visible stop action and private support. Never infer intent to harm from an OCD intrusive-thought response alone.

Before claiming clinical usefulness, conduct appropriate expert review, user comprehension testing, population-specific validation, and safety/privacy review. A syntactically valid JSON file is not a validated psychological assessment.

Before using other languages or age groups, review the content with appropriate experts and test the adapted version. English wording has not been validated for a Bangladeshi or any other target population.
referenceSourceUrl and sourceInstrument link to background sources. Where no source scoring page exists, additional_scoring_url repeats the background URL; it is not a scoring guide for Healer.
Treat method, formula, and trigger strings as specifications for developer implementation. Do not execute them using eval or a general-purpose expression interpreter.

assessments.timeframe: For dep_01 to dep_10, consider the past 14 days and choose how often each experience occurred. The two optional support questions state their own timeframe.

scoring.scoreDirection: Higher sums describe more frequent difficulty-related responses in this activity only.
scoring.missingAnswers: Compute a final summary only after all ten core questions are answered. A skipped, not-applicable, or cannot-judge response stays missing; do not replace it with zero, impute it, or prorate. Additional support questions are optional and excluded from the sum; evaluate any support answers immediately.
scoring.interpretationDisplay: Optional descriptive response sum: {score}/40. This new question set has no validated clinical interpretation or score bands.
scoring.note: Core question IDs: dep_01, dep_02, dep_03, dep_04, dep_05, dep_06, dep_07, dep_08, dep_09, dep_10. Describes selected experiences, not all diagnostic criteria. The support prompts dep_11 and dep_12 are excluded. No score can confirm depression or rule it out.

assessments.name: Personality Assessment
assessments.basedOn: Ten original statements organized by five broad personality domains; not a validated short IPIP scale, BFI, TIPI, or MBTI test.
assessments.timeframe: Think about your usual tendencies across situations over roughly the past six months, rather than a temporary mood. Choose your level of agreement.

scoring.scoreDirection: Higher component means describe more self-endorsed extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, emotional stability, or openness, respectively. Higher is not universally better.
scoring.missingAnswers: Display a component mean only when both questions in its specified pair are answered. Mark other components incomplete. Never fill missing answers with zero and never compute a global score.
scoring.interpretationDisplay: Display the five named component means separately, each from 0 to 4. These are tentative reflection prompts, not personality types or population percentiles.

There is no overall personality score. score(questionId) means the selected option score, already reverse-keyed. assessments.timeframe: Consider the past four weeks. Answer about unwanted or hard-to-resist experiences, not enjoyable routines, necessary hygiene, or freely chosen cultural or religious practices.

assessments.name: Autism Screening
assessments.basedOn: Original adult reflection prompts about communication, routines, interests, and sensory experiences, informed by NIMH guidance; not AQ-10 or another validated autism screen.
assessments.timeframe: Think about your usual experiences across your life, including earlier years when you can remember them. Choose how closely each statement describes you. You may skip any statement you cannot judge.

scoring.scoreDirection: A larger item code means that this particular statement feels more self-descriptive, not that a person is more autistic or more impaired.

assessments.name: IQ Test
assessments.basedOn: Original untimed reasoning-practice puzzles across number, verbal, spatial, and logical topics, conceptually informed by cognitive-assessment research. Not an IQ test.
assessments.timeframe: Complete the ten puzzles at your own pace. Choose one answer per puzzle. No time limit or speed score is used; these are educational reasoning exercises.

scoring.scoreDirection: Higher means more of these ten practice puzzles answered correctly, nothing more.
scoring.missingAnswers: A final score out of ten requires all ten answers. When incomplete, show progress and any requested explanations without treating omissions as wrong answers or producing a standardized result.
scoring.interpretationDisplay: Reasoning practice: {score} correct out of 10. This is not an IQ score, percentile, or estimate of general intelligence.
scoring.note: Core question IDs: iq_01, iq_02, iq_03, iq_04, iq_05, iq_06, iq_07, iq_08, iq_09, iq_10. Each correct answer has score 1 and each other answer 0. No age norms, reliability estimate, or IQ conversion exists. Provide answer explanations only after the user finishes or exits.

safetyRules.note: This original question is not an ASQ screen. Escalation needs depend on current circumstances and qualified assessment, not an automated risk label. A no or missing response does not establish safety.

safetyRules.name: current_self_harm_concern_support
actions: Interrupt ordinary result presentation with immediate support information; never display a reassuring score first.

safetyRules.note: Evaluate independently of dep_11 and all totals. Yes and unsure both open support, without assigning a suicide-risk category. A skipped or negative answer is not a safety clearance.

Advise not to drive or operate dangerous equipment while sleepy; use a safe alternative rather than continuing.

safetyRules.name: relationship_safety_support

show: The activity is unvalidated; show this before consent and alongside every result, not just in a footer.
The module name, response date, recall period, answered-item count, and the actual selected answers.
When all core items are complete, an optional raw sum with its denominator and the module-specific limitation; never call it a risk percentage.
For Personality, five separate component means from the specified pairs, each 0-4; for Autism, individual selected labels only.
For Reasoning practice, the number correct out of ten plus answer explanations, with no IQ conversion.
A supportive invitation to discuss persistent, distressing, or disruptive experiences with a qualified professional, regardless of any score.
Local, verified support options accessible at any time; an immediate support panel whenever a support trigger fires.
A privacy notice and clear Skip, Not applicable / Cannot judge, Stop, and delete-response controls.
doNotShow: Diagnoses, disorder probabilities, clinical screening positive/negative labels, or Mild/Moderate/Severe bands for these items.
A single combined mental-health score or rankings comparing different modules.
A low/medium/high suicide-risk label, reassurance of safety, or a guarantee of contacting a human.
An autism percentage, autism severity, level of support need, or statements that autism has been ruled in or out.
An IQ, mental age, percentile, giftedness label, or employment/educational recommendation based on the ten puzzles.
An overall good/bad personality score, MBTI type, diagnosis, or verified emotional intelligence quotient.
Published instrument cutoffs, validation claims, reliability estimates, or source-organization endorsements applied to these new items.
Medication advice, automated treatment plans, or instructions to start or stop prescribed treatment.
Sensitive results on lock screens, public leaderboards, shared profiles, or notifications visible to others.
